text:
lina.ops: Heads up — we started seeing a spike of 502s and connection_reset from edge proxies in us-east-1 around 09:02 UTC. Dash shows outbound ephemeral port utilization pegged. Suspect NATGW ephemeral port exhaustion + some short-lived model pull traffic. :eyes:

jamal_eng: Can you paste conntrack / netstat dump from one of the affected proxies?

lina.ops: Sure, grabbed one from proxy-ix-7:```
$ ss -tanp | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
87320
$ cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l
95000
# lots of TIME_WAIT and CLOSE_WAIT, high ephemeral port allocation
```

maria-sre: Interesting — that many TIME_WAITs would definitely drive SNAT reuse. If NATGW has only 3 ENIs/EIPs for that AZ we're in the danger zone (~64k ports per IP). When they wrap we see RST/502s. This matches model-pull bursts + infra healthchecks at the same time.

oliver-net: Quick checklist of mitigations: rotate additional EIPs onto the NAT gateway (adds ~64k ports each), move model pulls to VPC endpoint so they bypass NAT, or add an egress-multiplexing pool (sidecar HTTP keepalive pool). Longer term, we should avoid Connection: close from model fetchers.

jamal_eng: Edge-proxy config shows keepalive disabled for model-object fetches in v0.18.2 (we favored small per-request clients). We can flip to pooled http clients with 60s keepalive. That should cut ephemeral churn dramatically.

lina.ops: I'm starting a canary patch now: edge-proxy -> v0.18.3 with keepalive default on, connection pool size 200, and sysctl bump on proxy hosts: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 32768 65535 and net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max -> +50%. Will deploy to 5% traffic in us-east-1.

noah-infra: Question on cost: if we add NAT EIPs per AZ we'll increase charges. Is there a cheaper immediate lever? VPC endpoint for S3 model pulls is free data transfer within AZ but might require config changes in model-fetcher jobs.

maria-sre: Short-term cheapest wins: 1) route S3/model artifact pulls via s3 VPC endpoint; 2) enable keepalive/pooling in model-fetch clients; 3) increase conntrack and ephemeral range on proxies. Those reduce port churn without immediate extra NAT cost.

oliver-net: Also watch for conntrack table filling — TIME_WAIT isn't the only problem. If conntrack entries blow, packets get dropped earlier. We should alert on conntrack usage percent and per-node conntrack aging.

deploy-bot: deploy v0.18.3-canary -> edge-proxy/us-east-1 (proxy-ix-3, proxy-ix-7) started at 09:15 UTC by lina.ops

lina.ops: Canary results after 10m: 502/conn_reset spike in canary hosts dropped from ~18% of model requests to ~2%. Ephemeral port usage down ~65% on the canary hosts. Rolling to 25% next. :thumbsup:

jamal_eng: Nice. I'll open a follow-up to change model-puller libs to persistent http clients and add a test harness to simulate bursts.

noah-infra: I'll scope cost ops: add 2 extra EIPs to the NAT gateway as a fallback and create a runbook for rotating EIPs when port pressure crosses 80%.

maria-sre: Action items:
- patch model-puller clients (jamal)
- roll edge-proxy to keepalive globally (lina)
- add conntrack/ephemeral port alerts + dashboard (oliver)
- add s3 VPC endpoint routing for model fetches (noah)
- ticket for long-term egress multiplexing plan (infra-tech-debt)

lina.ops: Will do the roll and followups. Thanks everyone — looks like we avoided a larger outage. We'll keep the thread open until full rollout + NAT EIP fallback is in place. :white_check_mark:
